parsed.doc_summary: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Office page: states annual rent increase cap (lesser of 3% or 80% of CPI; 2.87% for 9/1/2026-8/31/2027), just cause eviction requirement, and relocation assistance.

rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - annual rent increase cap
rules.requirement: A landlord can raise rent only once a year by no more than the lesser of 3% or 80% of the CPI change. For 9/1/2026 through 8/31/2027 the maximum is 2.87%.
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: The increase cannot be more than 3% of your current rent or 80% of the Consumer Price Index (CPI) change, whichever is less.
rules.effective_date_note: Original effective date not stated in document.
rules.coverage_conditions: Exemptions not stated on this page.
rules.interaction: Local ordinance; state Tenant Protection Act rent cap yields to stricter local rent control.

rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance - just cause and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: A landlord must have a valid reason to evict, such as nonpayment, lease violation, or owner move-in. For certain no-fault evictions the landlord may have to help pay moving costs.
rules.key_value: Valid reason required; relocation assistance for certain evictions
rules.citation: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization and Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: Your landlord must have a valid reason to evict you. This could be for not paying rent, breaking the lease, or if the landlord wants to move into the property themselves.
rules.coverage_conditions: Exemptions not stated on this page.
